text:
Gyða Valtýsdóttir has been active as a musician since her early teens, as a founding member of the experimental pop group múm.

Classically trained, Gyða has made music for films, theatre and dance, among many other creative ventures, possessing a rare range of musical experiences which creates a unique alchemical compound.

Her music emerges from the fluidity of time and genres, dissolving any boundaries by simply not sensing their existence.

Her cello playing, always inventive and highly personal, underlines a dignified craftsmanship while flirting with sensitivity and strength.

Her list of collaborators is extensive and includes a wide palette of musicians and other artists, including Kronos Quartet, Aaron & Bryce Dessner, Josephine Foster, Damien Rice, Dustin O’Halloran, Colin Stetson, Kjartan Sveinsson and visual artist Ragnar Kjartansson, just to name a few.

◆

Gyða received the prestigious Nordic Council Music Prize 2019 for her music and performance, the jury calling her distinct vocals and instrumental inventiveness “highly unique and captivating”.

Her first solo album, Epicycle, came out in 2017 and received prestigious prizes at the Icelandic Music Awards. Epicycle is a constellation of written music spanning from ancient to avant-garde. A year later she released her first album of her own work, Evolution. The record was nominated for the Nordic Music Prize and won “Album of the Year” at the Icelandic Music Awards. The same year her first film soundtrack came out on the legendary Smekkleysa label, and was nominated for soundtrack of the year at the Icelandic Music Awards, at the Edda, the Icelandic film awards, and at the Nordic Film Composer awards.

In 2020 her third solo album, Epicycle II, came out on her own label DiaMond: a “genre-fluid” ode to collaboration and interconnection. On the album Gyða works with musicians who shaped her musical journey, such as Sigur Rós members Kjartan Sveinsson and Jónsi, who also mixed the album, composers Anna Thorvaldsdottir and Daníel Bjarnason, and others of Iceland’s most unique creatives.

Her fourth solo album, Ox, came out late in 2021. It is a visceral and wildly sublime, transcendental dance between inner and outer realms of existence. With its rich arrangements and intricate soundscapes, it celebrates the embodiment of both darkness and light through an open-heartedness that gives birth to writing that bursts with effortless originality.
